confirmed_facts.text: Government Decree 8-2026 declared a 30-day state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal from 14 November.
Congress ratified the measure on 17 November with 147 votes and authorised security forces to take control of prisons nationwide.

reported_claims.text: Two armed attacks on 13 November left seven people dead.
The interior minister said the government could analyse extending the state of siege to other departments.

unknowns: Whether violence has declined since the deployment

update_history.summary: Draft prepared for editorial review (sources accessed 23 November 2026).

title: Guatemala declares 30-day state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal after armed attacks
summary: Guatemala's government declared a 30-day state of siege in the eastern departments of Zacapa and Izabal on 14 November 2026 (Government Decree 8-2026) after armed attacks linked to drug-trafficking groups, deploying about 400 soldiers to Zacapa and 600 to Izabal. Congress ratified the measure on 17 November and authorised security forces to take control of prisons nationwide. The interior minister has said an extension to other departments could be considered.
impact_assessment: Observed: military deployment and restricted civil liberties in two departments. Potential: displacement of criminal activity to other areas and wider emergency measures.
priority_rationale: MODERATE: a confirmed national security emergency measure with regional drug-trafficking implications but geographically contained.
monitoring_actions: Track government and Congress decisions on extension
Watch violence indicators in neighbouring departments
